title: Multi-table Joins or Multi-way Unions in Transactional Queries
pattern: Creating highly complex handcrafted SQL queries involving many-way joins (e.g. 5+ tables) or multi-way `UNION` operations in transactional (OLTP) code paths.
why_bad: It creates extremely slow query plans that lock many tables simultaneously, causing database lock escalation, transactional timeouts, and blocking simple read/write operations.
detection: An SQL query containing more than 4 `JOIN` statements or multiple `UNION` operations executing inside a transactional, low-latency API endpoint.
counterexample: Complex joins executed inside a dedicated offline analytical (OLAP) reporting warehouse database.
fix: Split the query into simpler, targeted index-seeks, denormalize reporting data, or move complex analysis to a read-only secondary view.
